newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge up at close on inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge up at close on inflation data.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed earlier losses to close marginally up on Thursday after a late spurt due to better-than-expected inflation figures, traders said. They noted that the session was dull for most of the day as the market awaited the government's budget proposals, however.
"Inflation figures nudged the Bolsa up towards the close," a trader at the Bancomer brokerage said.
The blue chip IPC index ended 2.85 points up, or 0.09 percent, at 2,293.23. Volume was dull at 49.8 million shares traded and reflected a lack of investor interest in the market, traders said.

Banco de Mexico announced during late trade that consumer inflation for October was 1.25 percent, which was slightly below average expectations of 1.31 percent and the lowest monthly figure since the December 1994 peso crisis.
Thursday also saw 1997 budget proposals unveiled in congress, but said they failed to move a slothful market as they were much as expected.

"Budget guidelines were as expected, especially the forecast average exchange rate, which had caused some jitters," said another trader. The government expects the peso exchange rate to average 8.53 per dollar next year.
On the broad market, a total of 106 stocks changed hands, of which losers outnumbered winners by 50 to 33.

The losers list was dominated by three series of shares in financial firm GFInver. Traders said this was due to speculation ahead of an announcement of the subscription price for new shares to be issued to help finance the banking subsidiary's forthcoming acquisition by Banco Santander.
Holding company Gruma topped the leaders. Traders noted that Gruma recently placed $120 million of stock.
Traders felt that budget proposals could ease uncertainty and pave the way for gains on Friday.
"We could see a market with brighter prospects and livelier volume tomorrow, now that the uncertainty over budget proposals is behind us," the Bancomer trader said.
Technical analysts situated support and resistance at 3,262 and 3,326 points, respectively, with a pyschological barrier at 3,300 points.
